artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
Released in 1993 on Food Records (not Demon Records), Perverse is the third studio album by British rock band Jesus Jones. Musically, the album marked a significant shift toward electronic textures and production, embracing the emerging techno and dance-rock sounds of the early 1990s. Fronted by Mike Edwards, the band incorporated the Roland JD-800 synthesizer extensively, resulting in buzzing, metallic melodies and sawtoothed riffs that defined the album’s sonic character. Tracks like "Zeroes and Ones" and "The Devil You Know" exemplify this fusion of rock energy with electronic experimentation, positioning Perverse as an ambitious attempt to create a "techno rock" album that was both forward-thinking and rooted in alternative rock traditions.

Perverse stands as a pivotal release in Jesus Jones’ discography, representing the band’s first true realization of their own artistic vision after the more commercially driven Doubt. While previous albums were shaped by external expectations, Perverse reflected the band’s desire to innovate and assert their identity, with Edwards famously declaring it would be the first rock album for the 1990s. Commercially, the album debuted at number six in the UK and produced the US Modern Rock chart-topping single "The Devil You Know," though it ultimately underperformed compared to the massive success of Doubt. Despite its mixed critical reception and status as a commercial letdown, Perverse has since been recognized for its bold sonic experimentation and its role in bridging the gap between rock and electronic music in the early 1990s.
